Onus verbi Domini ad Israel: The burden of the word of the Lord to Israel
dicit Dominus, et dixistis: In quo dilex: saith the Lord: and you have said: Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau brother to Jacob, saith the Lord, and I have loved Jacob
Esau autem odio habui et posui montes ei: But have hated Esau? and I have made his mountains a wilderness, and given his inheritance to the dragons of the desert
Quod si dixerit Idumea, destructi: But if Edom shall say: We are destroyed
revertentes edificabimus: we will return and build up
que destructa sunt, hec dicit Dominus ex: what hath been destroyed: thus saith the Lord of hosts
Isti edificabunt et ego destruam et voca: They shall build up, and I will throw down: and they shall be called the borders of wickedness, and the people with whom the Lord is angry for ever
Filius honorat patrem et servus dominum: The son honoureth the father, and the servant his master: if then I be a father, where is my honour? and if I be a master, where is my fear? saith the Lord of hosts
qui despicitis nomen meum et dixistis: I: that despise my name, and have said: Wherein have we despised thy name?
Offertis super altare meum panem: You offer … bread upon my altar
offeratis cecum ad immolandum nonne malu: you offer the blind for sacrifice, is it not evil? and if you offer the lame and the sick
nonne malum est ? Offer illud duci tuo s: is it not evil? offer it to thy prince, if he will be pleased with it
aut si susceperit faciem tuam dicit Domi: or if he will regard thy face, saith the Lord of hosts
Et nunc deprecamini vultum Dei ut misere: And now beseech ye the face of God, that he may have mercy on you, (for by your hand hath this been done,)
si quomodo suscipiat facies vestras*, di: if by any means he will receive your faces, saith the Lord of hosts
Quis est in vobis qui claudat ostia: Who is there among you, that will shut the doors
et incendat altare meum gratuito ?: and will kindle the fire on my altar gratis?
Non est mihi voluntas in vobis, dicit Do: I have no pleasure in you, saith the Lord of hosts: and I will not receive a gift of your hand

magnum est nomen meum in gentibus: my name is great among the Gentiles
et* in omni loco sacrificatur et offertu: and in every place there is sacrifice, and there is offered
in eo quod dicitis: Mensa Domini contami: in that you say: The table of the Lord is defiled: and that which is laid thereupon is contemptible with the fire that devoureth it

fuit in ore eius et iniquitas non est in: was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found in his lips

and turned many away from iniquity

et legem requirent: and they shall seek the law
ex ore eius quia angelus Domini exercitu: at his mouth: because he is the angel of the Lord of hosts

et scandalizastis plurimos: and have caused many to stumble
in lege. Irritum fecistis pactum Levi: at the law: you have made void the covenant of Levi

omnibus populis sicut non servastis vias: before all people, as you have not kept my ways
Numquid non pater unus omnium nostrum ?: Have we not all one father?
Numquid non unus Deus creavit nos ? Quar: hath not one God created us? why then doth every one of us despise his brother, violating the covenant of our fathers?
et abominatio facta est in Israel et in: and abomination hath been committed in Israel, and in Jerusalem: for Juda hath profaned

ita ut ultra non respiciam: so that I have no more a regard

et preparabit viam ante faciem meam: and he shall prepare the way before my face
et statim veniet ad templum suum: And presently … shall come to his temple

maleficis et adulteris et periuris: against sorcerers, and adulterers, and false swearers

et revertar ad vos dicit Dominus exercit: and I will return to you, saith the Lord of hosts. And you have said

omnem decimam in horreum meum: all the tithes into the storehouse
et sit cibus in domo mea et probate me s: that there may be meat in my house, and try me in this, saith the Lord: if I open not unto you the flood-gates of heaven
et increpabo pro vobis: And I will rebuke for your sakes

quia custodivimus precepta eius et quia: that we have kept his ordinances, and that we have walked sorrowful

timentes Deum unusquisque cum proximo su: they that feared the Lord … every one with his neighbour
